Q020.reason: The Marshall Plan (1948) was the American program of economic aid to rebuild postwar Europe; the 1947 Greece/Turkey aid was the Truman Doctrine.

Q021.reason: NSC 68 (1950) called for a large military buildup, marking a shift from economic toward military containment, contrary to the shared note.

Q022.reason: The Monroe Doctrine (1823) warned European powers to stay out of the Western Hemisphere; Theodore Roosevelt's early-1900s corollary expanded it, not originated it.

Q023.reason: Truman's 1947 speech framed aid to Greece and Turkey as a general commitment to support free peoples resisting subjugation, which is widely read as a global containment principle, though the shared note argues it was narrower.

Q024.reason: A multipolar system has three or more major powers; the shared note's definition of exactly two describes bipolarity.
